observation.visible_scene: A curvy, hurricane-shaped transparent glass stands centered against a pure black background, filled to near the rim with a clear, effervescent liquid. A single red strawberry with a green calyx is fully submerged in the lower-middle portion of the glass, surrounded by a dense cluster of small bubbles. Numerous bubbles rise through the liquid column, and the top meniscus shows a thin foamy layer.
visible_changes: In the first several frames (t=0.00–0.48 s) a few small bright water droplets fall vertically outside the glass, mainly on the left side and occasionally on the right; these droplets move downward and are no longer visible by about t=0.56–0.64 s.

The submerged strawberry drifts slowly upward within the glass: its center moves from a lower-middle position at t=0.00 s to a higher-middle position by t=3.20 s, while the glass itself stays at a fixed position in the frame.
The strawberry also rotates slightly over time, with its green calyx shifting from pointing upward early in the clip to pointing toward the upper-left in later frames.

The bubble field around the strawberry and throughout the liquid continuously changes—bubbles form, detach, and rise—so the white frothy coating around the fruit and the streaks of bubbles in the upper liquid are in constant, non-uniform motion.
The liquid surface at the top of the glass shows small, ongoing shape changes in the meniscus/foam layer.
outside_clip_unknowns: What placed the strawberry in the glass and whether it was dropped or already present before the segment.
The source or trajectory of the external falling droplets seen only at the start.
Whether the strawberry continues to rise, reaches the surface, or stops after t=3.20 s.
The identity of the liquid (only inferred visually as a carbonated clear liquid).
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be confirmed because the background is uniformly black; the glass appears stationary relative to the frame, but any slight global shift is indistinguishable.
It is not certain whether the new bubbles are nucleating on the strawberry's surface or merely passing by it.
The exact rotation axis/direction of the strawberry is approximate, derived from the calyx orientation across frames.
